;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]], [[Central Libya offensive (2020)]]
**The speaker of the Libyan [[House of Representatives (Libya)|House of Representatives]], [[Aguila Saleh Issa]], asks [[Egypt]] to intervene in [[Libya]] if the armed forces of the [[Government of National Accord]] attempt to capture the city of [[Sirte]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/libya-aguila-saleh-urges-egypt-intervene-sirte-attacked-200624180955293.html (Al Jazeera)]
;Business and economy
*[[Segway Inc.]] announces that production of its [[personal transporter]] will end on July 15. Production began in 2001. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-53160518 (BBC News)]
*[[Bayer|Bayer AG]] announces it has agreed to pay [[United States dollar|US$]]10 billion to resolve thousands of lawsuits regarding claims that the [[Monsanto]] [[herbicide]] [[Roundup (herbicide)|Roundup]] causes [[cancer]]. Court-appointed mediator [[Kenneth Feinberg]] says the deal is a "constructive and reasonable" resolution. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/bayer-reaches-10-5-billion-settlement-roundup-cancer-lawsuits-n1232026 (NBC News)]
*[[Japan]]ese manufacturing company [[Olympus Corporation|Olympus]] announces it is exiting the [[camera]] business after 84 years, stating its financial losses caused by their inability to compete with [[smartphone]] cameras was a major factor in the decision. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-53165293 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**The [[North Korea]]n state news agency [[Korean Central News Agency|KCNA]] reports that the country will suspend military action plans against the [[South Korea|South]] after a meeting of the [[Central Military Commission of the Workers' Party of Korea|Central Military Commission]] presided by [[Kim Jong-un]]. North Korea had protested against [[North Korean defectors|defectors]] sending leaflets to the border, and Kim's sister [[Kim Yo-jong]] had threatened a military response. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/korea-kim-suspends-plans-military-action-south-200624004316030.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
**[[List of ambassadors of the European Union|Ambassadors for EU member states]] meet today to develop criteria for reopening external borders to travelers on July 1. [[European Commission]] guidance is that non-[[EU]] countries whose [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] status, e.g., the number of new infections, the trend in new infections, and testing and tracing, are comparable or better than the EU average will make the safe list. Other factors, such as reciprocity and links to the EU, will also be considered. Travelers from countries such as [[Brazil]], [[Russia]], and the [[United States]] may be barred based on these rules. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53161447 (BBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/world/europe/coronavirus-EU-American-travel-ban.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]; [[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**U.S. Secretary of State [[Mike Pompeo]] announces sanctions on five [[Iranian peoples|Iranian]] ship captains who delivered fuel to [[Venezuela]] and reaffirms support for disputed President [[Juan Guaidó]] over [[Nicolás Maduro]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-iran-gasoline/u-s-sanctions-five-iranian-ship-captains-for-bringing-oil-to-venezuela-pompeo-idUSKBN23V25I?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[War crimes in the Kosovo War]]
**The [[Kosovo Specialist Chambers and Specialist Prosecutor's Office|Specialist Prosecutor's Office]] announces that it has submitted for court approval an indictment against [[President of Kosovo|President]] [[Hashim Thaçi]] and nine other former [[Kosovo Liberation Army]] fighters alleging that they committed [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]] during the [[Kosovo War]]. Following the announcement, President Thaçi cancels his upcoming trip to the [[United States]]. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/europe/kosovo-s-president-indicted-for-war-crimes-withdraws-from-white-house-talks-20200625-p555wq.html (''Sydney Morning Herald'')]
*[[George Floyd protests]]
** The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] fails to invoke [[cloture]] on a 55–45 vote effectively tabling a [[Police brutality in the United States|police misconduct]] bill introduced by the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]], after the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] argued that it did not do enough to incentivize change. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-minneapolis-police-congress/senate-police-reform-vote-fails-as-democrats-reject-republican-bill-idUSKBN23V1G2?il=0 (Reuters)]
**Leaders of the [[Capitol Hill Autonomous Zone]] announce the zone's disestablishment. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/24/us/seattle-autonomous-zone-protesters-leaving/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Mongolian legislative election]]
**[[Mongolia]]n voters head to the polls to elect the members of the [[State Great Khural]]. A record number of more than 600 candidates are competing for the 76 seats in the parliament. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-06-23/mongolia-s-future-as-oasis-of-democracy-put-to-election-test (Bloomberg)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
*Former [[Boston Red Sox]] player [[Eddie Kasko]] dies at age 88. [https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-red-sox/2020/06/25/eddie-kasko-red-sox-obituary/amp (Boston)]
**[[2020 Major League Baseball season]]
***[[Major League Baseball]] Commissioner [[Rob Manfred]] unilaterally implements a 60-game season. Players will report to training camps on July 1 in order to resume [[spring training]] and prepare for a July 23 or 24 [[Opening Day]]. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/29354014/sources-mlbpa-agrees-report-july-1-discussing-health-safety-protocols (ESPN)]
*English football club [[Leeds United F.C.]] issue an apology after a [[cardboard cutout]] of former [[al-Qaeda]] leader [[Osama bin Laden]] was displayed in the stands at their [[Elland Road]] stadium. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=12342840 (''The New Zealand Herald'')] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53171423 (BBC Sport)]
